targets.text: AgentCulture has one direct agent control plane (culture-agents), one communication product (culture-chat), one workflow engine (culture-rules), and independently deployable experience apps (embodiment/Gwen): no duplicated harness or dispatch managers, no requirement that agents join chat, and no lost realtime or safety guarantees.
The exported spec covers only D0 plus D1; the announcement's later parts (culture-chat, culture-rules, embodiment) are listed as deferred, not claimed as delivered.

Every D-gate is tracked on issue #2 with a linked receiving-repo issue, the consumer that exercises it, and the result required before cutover (issue #2 comment 1, closing paragraph). No such receiving-repo issues exist yet.
Each sibling repo with a later gate has one open issue linking culture-agents#2, naming the gate, the consumer that exercises it and the result required before cutover.

Sibling-repo changes for this work are made only in dedicated per-repo worktrees on work-scoped branches and land through PRs; primary sibling checkouts, their uncommitted work and their current branches are never touched.
git status in every primary sibling checkout is byte-identical before and after this work.

D0 produces, in culture-agents, the inventory and contract that do not exist today: a consumer/feature inventory of agentirc, cultureagent and agent-lifecycle; a compatibility matrix with an owner and disposition per installed path; run/task/session/event schemas; the auth model; and the TS-vs-Python seam decision (issue #2, D0 and Decisions 1-6).
docs/d0/ holds the inventory, the compatibility matrix with an owner and disposition per installed path, and a decision record for each of issue #2's six D0 decisions, each marked decided or open.

The reorganization keeps the distributed mesh while dropping the IRC wire format: culture-agents and culture-chat share the <node>-<agent> identity namespace, mesh.yaml topology, grant-backed credentials and per-peer anti-spoofing, so an agent has a verifiable mesh identity without joining chat (issue #2 comment 2, section 1; confirmed in comment 3, item 2).
Agent and run identifiers in the D1 schemas carry the <node>-<agent> form read from server.yaml and culture.yaml, and D1 works when no server.yaml chat section is reachable.

culture-agents separates a per-run worker shim (PID/control socket, event cursor, pending operator question persisted on disk) from the control-plane daemon, so restarting the daemon reconnects to live runs instead of orphaning them (issue #2 comment 2 section 2; Acceptance Test 2).
Each run executes in its own worker process that writes its PID, event log and cursor to disk before the daemon acknowledges the submit.

D1 steer and answer are built on interactive harness transports (codex app-server JSON-RPC, ACP for qwen/opencode, claude-agent-sdk streaming input, or checkpoint plus --resume), because the existing bridges are one-shot (issue #2 comment 2 section 2; comment 3 item 6).
Each D1 harness is driven through an interactive session transport, and the D0 matrix names that transport per harness.

The D0 compatibility matrix covers colleague, qwen (qwen --acp) and associate (the Pi wrapper with the CLEF gate) alongside Claude, Codex, OpenCode and Pi, plus the three hand-rolled raw IRC clients (irc-lens, codexd, embodiment mesh_client.py) enumerated by wire behavior (issue #2 comment 2 section 3 item 4; comment 3 item 9 and qualifier 3).
The matrix has a row for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi (via associate), colleague and qwen, each with its transport, capabilities, D1 status and the three raw IRC clients listed for D3.

AI-SDK types never appear in the public contract: the JSON schemas, CLI output and event stream are harness-neutral, so swapping the Vercel AI SDK for another harness runtime leaves them unchanged (issue #2 comment 4 litmus test). The Python side keeps the 400-line file cap, and each runtime dependency beyond agentfront needs the user's approval.
Replacing one harness adapter with a stub that imports no AI-SDK package leaves every contract and CLI test passing unchanged.

The workspace-level /home/ori/git/CLAUDE.md is rewritten to describe the reorganized product map; today it names none of the 14 repos issue #2 touches and still calls culture an 'IRC-based agent mesh'.
The culture repo has a merged or open PR adding the product and repo map, and /home/ori/git/CLAUDE.md points to it.

embodiment's mesh client, voice fast path and dashboard are not changed before D3/D5: turn.py's loop_run call stays byte-unchanged, loop.py keeps its no-subprocess posture, and any culture-agents client inside embodiment is stdlib-only (or uses the already-approved websockets>=15).
No file under embodiment/ changes in this work.

D0's inventory is taken against current upstream main of each repo, not the local checkouts the issue-2 verification pass used: cultureagent is 0.17.0 upstream (local 0.15.2), agentirc 9.14.0 (local 9.12.0) and irc-lens 0.23.0 (local 0.21.0), and the missing commits change files inside the move scope.
Every file:line citation in docs/d0/ resolves against the upstream main commit SHA recorded at the top of the inventory.

D1 changes nothing in cultureagent or agent-lifecycle: their published contracts (bridge HTTP API /v1/invocations, result schema cultureagent.bridge.result/v1, console scripts, agent_lifecycle.runtime import paths) and all current consumers keep working, and code is cited into culture-agents, never moved out.
No commit is pushed to cultureagent or agent-lifecycle by this work.

Operators and agents that need to hand work to a coding-agent harness on one host without a chat server: the human operator at the 'agents' CLI, and programmatic callers (other agents, later embodiment and culture-rules) using the same control API.
A caller with no IRC or culture-chat client configured can complete submit, show, attach, steer and cancel end to end.

culture-agents is a template scaffold with no control-plane code. Dispatch exists only as cultureagent's one-shot bridges, which cannot steer or answer and report an in-flight run as unknown after a restart, and as IRC-coupled resident daemons that need the chat server up to start.
The D0 inventory records these gaps against upstream main of cultureagent and culture, not the stale local checkouts.

On a single host, 'agents runs submit' hands a task to a TS core daemon and returns a durable run ID; the run can be listed, shown, attached to as a live event stream, steered mid-run and cancelled, against real harnesses, with no chat server running; run state is stored on disk and read back truthfully after the daemon restarts.
Every state shown after a daemon restart was read from disk or from a live worker; a run whose outcome cannot be established reads 'unknown', never 'succeeded'.

With no chat server process running: submit returns a run ID in < 2 seconds; at least 2 real harnesses complete a submitted task; a steer sent mid-run changes the run's subsequent output in 1 of 1 scripted trials per steer-capable harness; cancel reaches the terminal state 'cancelled' in < 10 seconds; and after kill -9 of the daemon plus restart, 100% of previously submitted runs report a state and 0 report an invented success.
The measurements come from a recorded run on the real fleet host, with harness versions logged, not from mocks.

The control-plane contract is a set of versioned JSON Schemas in this repo for agent, session, run, control action and event, with stable IDs, caller/owner, idempotency key, deadline, explicit terminal states (succeeded, failed, cancelled, timed_out, unknown), a transport-independent event cursor and a per-harness capability document; both the TS core and the Python CLI validate against the same files.
A contract test fails the build if either side emits or accepts a payload the schemas reject, and no schema references an AI-SDK type name.

Capability reporting is honest: each harness adapter declares whether it supports steer, cancel, resume and operator questions; a control action the harness cannot perform is refused with a typed 'unsupported' error naming the capability, never silently dropped or simulated.
For every harness in D1, each declared capability is exercised by a live test, and each undeclared one is shown to be refused.

The 'agents' CLI gains the noun groups 'agents agents list|status' and 'agents runs submit|list|show|attach|steer|cancel|logs|result', built on agentfront, each with --json, an explain entry and the exit-code contract (0 ok, 1 user error, 2 environment error); the scaffold drift is fixed in the same change (prog name 'agents', template wording in learn/explain and AGENTS.override.md).
With the core daemon stopped, every runs verb exits 2 with a remediation hint and no traceback.

Dispatch authority defaults to deny and is enforced by the core, not by a prompt: in D1 the control socket is owner-only (mode 0600) and a submit must name an agent, harness and repo that appear in an explicit local allow-list, which ships empty.
A fresh install refuses every submit until the operator adds an allow-list entry, and text inside a task, memory record or harness output cannot add one.

All five harness prompt files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, AGENTS.override.md, AGENTS.colleague.md, QWEN.md) and the harness-smoke config are updated together to describe the TS core, the new build and test commands and the agentfront dependency.
harness-smoke's config stage passes for all five harnesses after the change.

Every npm dependency of the TS core is pinned to an exact version with a committed lockfile, and an upgrade of any @ai-sdk/* or vendor SDK package is its own PR that re-runs the live D1 acceptance stage.
package.json contains no range specifier for a runtime dependency and CI installs with the lockfile frozen.

In D1 the core starts at most one active run per repository path and refuses a second with a typed 'busy' error; the harness never receives the operator's GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN or SSH_AUTH_SOCK, and a push to the remote is denied, enforced by the OpenShell sandbox policy and credential providers.
A second submit against a repo with a live run is refused, and a harness told to push leaves the remote branch unchanged.

The core daemon is single-instance per user: it takes an exclusive lock before binding the control socket, removes a stale socket left by a killed daemon, and a second start exits with an environment error naming the running instance.
After kill -9 the daemon restarts without manual cleanup, and starting it twice leaves exactly one process bound to the socket.

CI and release cover the TS core: tests.yml gains Node build, type-check, lint and unit-test jobs and Sonar includes the TS sources; the 400-line cap and the secret scan apply to TS files; and an npm publish job runs as a dry-run on PRs and publishes on main.
A PR that breaks the TS build or adds a 401-line TS file fails CI, and a PR run shows an npm publish dry-run.

D1 runs each harness through the AI SDK harness adapters inside an NVIDIA OpenShell sandbox: culture-agents implements the AI SDK's sandbox-session interface on top of the official OpenShell TypeScript SDK (@ai-openshell/sdk), because no OpenShell provider for the AI SDK exists, and the OpenShell policy and credential providers, not environment scrubbing alone, bound what a run can reach.
A run started through the core is visible as an OpenShell sandbox on the gateway, and a command inside it that the policy denies (for example a push to the remote) fails.

The first build task is a time-boxed probe on this host, before any other core code: install OpenShell, start Claude Code and Codex through the AI SDK adapters in an OpenShell sandbox, and record whether submit, streamed output, mid-run steer and cancel work; if steer or the sandbox bridge fails for a harness, that harness falls back to its vendor SDK behind the same adapter interface and the capability document says so.
docs/d0/ contains the probe log with package versions and a pass, fail or not-verified result per harness and per capability.

tasks.summary: Control-plane contract: versioned JSON Schemas and a contract test kit
acceptance_criteria: Every fixture under contract/fixtures/valid validates and every one under invalid is rejected, in a pytest run
A test fails if any schema contains an AI-SDK, OpenShell or vendor-SDK type name
Agent and run identifiers in the schemas carry the node-agent form and validation passes with no chat server configured
tasks.instruction: Create contract/ with one schema per entity (agent, session, run, control-action, event, capabilities, error) and contract/fixtures/ with valid and invalid examples. Identifiers use the node-agent form. Terminal states: succeeded, failed, cancelled, timed_out, unknown. Harness-specific data only in one opaque extension field. Add a Python test that validates every fixture; the TS side reuses the same fixtures in its own task.

tasks.summary: Core daemon: control socket, single-instance lock, API version and deny-by-default authorization
acceptance_criteria: After kill -9 the daemon restarts without manual cleanup, and a second start exits with an environment error naming the running instance

The socket file is mode 0600 and the version endpoint returns the API version from the contract
tasks.instruction: Files under core/src/daemon/ only. Unix socket with mode 0600 in the user runtime dir; exclusive lock taken before bind; stale socket removed only after the lock is held; GET version endpoint; allow-list read from the user config dir, shipped empty. Test-first against the contract fixtures.

tasks.instruction: Files under core/src/store/ and core/src/worker/ only. The worker is a separate OS process that writes PID, event log and cursor under the run directory with 0600 files; the store derives state only from those files or a live worker. Test-first, with a fake harness.

Ship one policy file that denies pushes to the remote and passes no operator GitHub or SSH credentials. Unit tests use a fake gateway; one live test is skipped and reported NOT VERIFIED when no gateway is reachable.

risks.text: Working-tree handoff between the host repository and the OpenShell sandbox (clone and fetch back, mount, or mirror) is undecided; the user picks from the probe's results before the sandbox provider is built.
risks.resolution: User 2026-11-25: option B from docs/d0/probe.md. Git bundle in, clone inside the sandbox, host fetches over SSH into runs/<id>.

risks.text: HarnessAgent may not expose mid-run steering for Claude Code or Codex; the fallback is the vendor SDK behind the same adapter interface for that harness.
OpenShell is alpha and its TypeScript SDK was first published 2026-11-24; an API change can break the sandbox provider between pinned upgrades.
(Applies to the boundary audit, t17.) Sibling primary checkouts are in active use, so the before/after comparison can show differences this work did not cause.
